issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for GroverLightsOutPuzzle: the template declares __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) while the solution implements __init__(self) with no parameter. This is inconsistent with the template's own run() example and the surrounding usage (the run() helper and grover_circuit expect the initial board passed to grover_circuit, not to the constructor). Students will be confused which constructor signature to implement and whether an initial_state should be supplied at construction time or passed to grover_circuit; this inconsistency can block or mislead implementations and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across template and solution. Either remove the initial_state parameter from the template __init__ signature (so both template and solution use __init__(self)), or update the solution to accept initial_state and propagate it to instance state. Also update the run() example and docstrings so they consistently show how the initial board should be provided (either at construction or when calling grover_circuit).

issues.description: Constructor/API mismatch for the Lights Out puzzle class: the template declares GroverLightsOutPuzzle.__init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) (expecting an initial_state parameter) while the solution implements GroverLightsOutPuzzle.__init__(self) with no parameter. The rest of the exercise API (state_of_lights passed to state_preparation/grover_circuit and the example in the problem text) consistently uses the name state_of_lights. This inconsistency in constructor signature and parameter naming across artifacts can confuse students about where and how to provide the initial board state.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor API consistent across template and solution and align the parameter name with the rest of the exercise. Either (A) change the template __init__ to def __init__(self): (no parameter) and pass state_of_lights explicitly to state_preparation/grover_circuit (as in the solution), or (B) update the solution to accept def __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) and store/use initial_state (or rename initial_state to state_of_lights) so that all artifacts use the same initializer signature and parameter name.
